title: A Goodwill work order is created No Charge with no original asked
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, with one asset, asset 1.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Work Order.
  2. Pick customer A.
  3. Pick asset 1.
  4. Tick the "No Charge" checkbox.
  5. Pick "Goodwill" in Category.
  6. Click Save in the New Work Order window.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 2:

  • Customer A is picked.

Step 3:

  • Asset 1 is picked.

Step 4:

  • The Category select appears.

Step 5:

  • No "Original work order" select appears.

Step 6:

  • The work order opens with one "No Charge" badge next to its status.
  • The category is not shown on the work order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R2: “In the New Work Order dialog (New Work Order only; Edit Work Order, which shares the dialog, is unchanged), picking a customer without the flag shows, at the bottom of the dialog below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and separated from it by a divider, an unticked checkbox "No Charge" with an info icon whose tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." Ticking it reveals the required select "Category" listing the active No Charge categories, empty by default; Save is refused with the field message "Pick a category" until one is picked. When the category requires the original work order, the select "Original work order" appears under it (the customer's invoiced and closed work orders at the locations the user has access to, those on the same asset first, each as number, date and first line, and "Not in ShopView" under Other), optional here, with the helper "Which earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView, and the line on it. The line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers. Optional here, required at Close."; once a work order is picked, the optional select "Original line" lists its lines (number, title, technician). The checkbox is hidden when the selected customer is an internal customer and for users without 'See Financial Data'. Ticked, the work order is created No Charge with that category. It works whether or not any customer is flagged. As soon as a work order or a line is picked, the line "Original technician: [names]" (or "Original technician: none") shows under the selects, so a wrong attribution is seen and corrected by picking the line before anything is saved.”
  • S2-R3: “The work order header shows one badge next to the status: "Internal" for an internal work order, "No Charge" for a no-charge work order (a different style from Internal), in the desktop and the mobile header. It is the only mark on the work order: the customer card on the detail page shows no badge and no category. On the detail page the header card of an internal or no-charge work order has an orange outline and a light orange background (a new style for the header card, on desktop and on the mobile header; the design authority names the token), so the work order is recognised at a glance; there is no hint sentence under the header. The category of a no-charge work order is not shown on the work order; it is in the Change category dialog, on the NO CHARGE document and in the report (S2-R16). A billable work order that carries no-charge lines carries no badge and no header style; the line carries the mark (Story 12).”
  • S2-R16: “A no-charge work order always carries one category from the No Charge list, set at creation (S2-R2) or at conversion (S2-R5) and editable with Change category (S2-R6) until Close. It shows in the Change category dialog, on the NO CHARGE document and the estimate under the masthead ("Category: Warranty", with "· Original work order S2-30455" only when the original is a real work order, never "Not in ShopView"), in the notes and the audit log, in the Internal Work Orders report (S9-R2), in the Customer Invoice export (S9-R6), in the hub record (S8-R1) and in the Open API (S2-R12). It is not shown on the work order detail or in lists; the badge is the only mark there. The category decides the account the parts cost posts to (Stories 5 to 8). Internal work orders carry an Internal category resolved by S2-R1.”
  • Terminology: “No-charge work order → a work order on a regular customer marked No Charge at creation or converted from the menu, with a category from the shop's list (Warranty, Goodwill and Comeback to start). Same behaviour as an internal work order, different expense account, history stays on the customer.”
  • Key Decisions: “Goodwill, comebacks, policy and warranty work on a customer's unit are one No Charge mark on that customer's work order, with a category, set at creation or switched from the three-dots menu; not a discount and not a customer flag.”
